who.en:
Sukari is the box for an adult living with diabetes, on tablets or on insulin. Diabetes is managed at home, between clinic visits: by measuring, by caring for the feet, by being ready for a low sugar and by taking every dose. In Tanzania’s 2023 national STEPS survey, 2.9% of adults aged 18–69 had diabetes, rising to 6.5% at ages 46–69, and 72.4% of those found to have it had never been diagnosed; only 17.2% were diagnosed and on medication. Many people therefore start treatment late, with damage to the eyes, feet and kidneys already under way.

The box follows WHO’s HEARTS-D module for type 2 diabetes in primary care and the ADA Standards of Care 2025 for monitoring, hypoglycaemia and foot, eye, kidney and dental checks, with the IWGDF 2023 guideline for foot ulcer prevention. The first box brings the meter, logbook, pill box, nail clipper and sharps box that last for years. Every box after it brings what is used up: test strips sized to the clinic’s testing plan, one lancet per strip, foot cream, soap for washing before each test and glucose for a low; on insulin also one needle per injection.

The number of strips follows a stated formula: tests a week set by the clinic × weeks covered + 5 spare, rounded up to whole packs. The default plans are 4 tests a week on tablets and 16 a week on insulin; if the clinic sets another plan, the next box changes. The strip brand always follows the meter, because strips fit only their own meter.

Tablets, insulin and rehydration salts are medicines. They are listed so the routine is complete, but Afya does not sell or price them: the licensed partner pharmacy supplies them on the clinic’s prescription.
who.sw:
Sukari ni sanduku la mtu mzima anayeishi na kisukari, anayetumia vidonge au insulini. Kisukari hudhibitiwa nyumbani, kati ya ziara za kliniki: kwa kupima, kutunza miguu, kujiandaa sukari ikishuka na kumeza kila dozi. Katika utafiti wa kitaifa wa STEPS wa 2023 nchini Tanzania, asilimia 2.9 ya watu wazima wenye umri wa miaka 18–69 walikuwa na kisukari, ikipanda hadi asilimia 6.5 kwa umri wa miaka 46–69, na asilimia 72.4 ya waliokutwa nacho walikuwa hawajawahi kugunduliwa; ni asilimia 17.2 tu waliokuwa wamegunduliwa na wanatumia dawa. Hivyo wengi huanza matibabu wakiwa wamechelewa, macho, miguu na figo vikiwa tayari vimeanza kuathirika.

Sanduku linafuata moduli ya WHO HEARTS-D kuhusu kisukari aina ya pili katika huduma ya msingi na ADA Standards of Care 2025 kuhusu upimaji, sukari kushuka na uchunguzi wa miguu, macho, figo na meno, pamoja na mwongozo wa IWGDF wa 2023 wa kuzuia vidonda vya miguu. Sanduku la kwanza huleta kipimo, daftari, kisanduku cha vidonge, kikata kucha na kisanduku cha sindano vinavyodumu kwa miaka. Kila sanduku linalofuata huleta kinachotumika: vipande vya kupimia kulingana na mpango wa kliniki, sindano ndogo moja kwa kila kipande, krimu ya miguu, sabuni ya kunawa kabla ya kupima na glukosi ya sukari ikishuka; kwa wanaotumia insulini pia sindano moja kwa kila dozi.

Idadi ya vipande hufuata kanuni iliyoelezwa: vipimo kwa wiki vilivyowekwa na kliniki × wiki zinazohusika + 5 vya ziada, vikizungushwa juu hadi pakiti nzima. Mipango ya kawaida ni vipimo 4 kwa wiki kwa vidonge na 16 kwa wiki kwa insulini; kliniki ikiweka mpango mwingine, sanduku linalofuata hubadilika. Chapa ya vipande hufuata kipimo kila mara, kwa sababu vipande hufaa kipimo chake tu.

Vidonge, insulini na chumvi za kurejesha maji ni dawa. Zimeorodheshwa ili utaratibu ukamilike, lakini Afya haiziuzi wala kuziwekea bei: famasia mshirika yenye leseni huzitoa kwa maelekezo ya kliniki.

clinic_line.en: How often you test your sugar, your targets, your tablets or insulin and their doses, and what to do on a sick day are decided by your clinic. Afya does not sell medicines: the licensed partner pharmacy supplies them only on the clinic’s prescription. A wound on the foot, a low that does not recover with glucose, or vomiting on insulin goes to the clinic the same day.
clinic_line.sw: Mara ngapi upime sukari, malengo yako, vidonge au insulini na dozi zake, na la kufanya siku ya kuugua huamuliwa na kliniki yako. Afya haiuzi dawa: famasia mshirika yenye leseni huzitoa tu kwa maelekezo ya kliniki. Jeraha mguuni, sukari iliyoshuka isiyopanda baada ya glukosi, au kutapika ukiwa kwenye insulini, nenda kliniki siku hiyo hiyo.

why.en: Used lancets and needles thrown loose into household rubbish injure family members, children and waste collectors. why.en: Some tablets, notably glibenclamide and other sulfonylureas still widely used in Tanzania, can push sugar too low, especially when a meal is missed. The rule is 15 g of fast glucose, a recheck after 15 minutes and a repeat if still below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), then a snack (ADA 2025, as cited earlier). why.en: Diabetes dries the skin of the feet, and cracked heels let infection in through skin that may no longer feel pain. Plain petroleum jelly does the job; urea creams are offered for thick, cracked heels.

why.en: Diarrhoea, vomiting or fever is when diabetes turns dangerous: fluid loss pushes sugar up, and some tablets, such as metformin, may need to be paused while the body is dry. ORS is a medicine in Tanzania (R1), so the partner pharmacy supplies it; WHO low-osmolarity ORS is mixed exactly as the sachet says.

name.en: Insulin pen needles (or syringes for vials)
name.sw: Sindano za kalamu ya insulini (au sindano za chupa)

why.en: A pen needle or syringe is made for one injection: reused needles blunt and damage the tissue under the skin, where lumps form and insulin is absorbed unpredictably. Short needles (4–5 mm) are enough for most adults and lower the risk of injecting into muscle. Pen or vial, and the insulin strength, are the clinic’s choice. A syringe must match the insulin strength: 40 IU/ml insulin, common in Tanzania, needs U-40 syringes; the partner pharmacy checks this with the prescription.

Sindano fupi (mm 4–5) zinatosha kwa watu wazima wengi na hupunguza hatari ya kudunga kwenye msuli. Kalamu au chupa, na nguvu ya insulini, ni uamuzi wa kliniki. Sindano ya chupa lazima ilingane na nguvu ya insulini: insulini ya IU 40/ml, inayotumika sana Tanzania, inahitaji sindano za U-40; famasia mshirika huhakiki hili pamoja na maelekezo ya daktari.

name.en: Insulin pen needles (or syringes for vials)
name.sw: Sindano za kalamu ya insulini (au sindano za chupa)

why.en: A pen needle or syringe is made for one injection: reused needles blunt and damage the tissue under the skin, where lumps form and insulin is absorbed unpredictably. Short needles (4–5 mm) are enough for most adults and lower the risk of injecting into muscle. Pen or vial, and the insulin strength, are the clinic’s choice. A syringe must match the insulin strength: 40 IU/ml insulin, common in Tanzania, needs U-40 syringes; the partner pharmacy checks this with the prescription.
why.sw: Sindano ya kalamu au ya chupa imetengenezwa kwa sindano moja tu: sindano zinazorudiwa hupoteza ukali na kuharibu nyama chini ya ngozi, ambako uvimbe hutokea na insulini hufyonzwa bila mpangilio. Sindano fupi (mm 4–5) zinatosha kwa watu wazima wengi na hupunguza hatari ya kudunga kwenye msuli. Kalamu au chupa, na nguvu ya insulini, ni uamuzi wa kliniki. Sindano ya chupa lazima ilingane na nguvu ya insulini: insulini ya IU 40/ml, inayotumika sana Tanzania, inahitaji sindano za U-40; famasia mshirika huhakiki hili pamoja na maelekezo ya daktari.

name.en: Sharps box for used lancets and needles

why.en: Used lancets and needles thrown loose into household rubbish injure family members, children and waste collectors. A rigid, puncture-proof box with a lid, kept out of children’s reach and sealed when three-quarters full, is the safe way (US FDA guidance on home sharps, as cited earlier; not re-opened). Ask the clinic or dialysis unit where the sealed box is accepted; do not put it in recycling.

name.sw: Krimu ya miguu kwa ngozi kavu

why.en: Diabetes dries the skin of the feet, and cracked heels let infection in through skin that may no longer feel pain. The IWGDF 2023 guideline on preventing foot ulcers advises checking the feet every day, washing and drying carefully between the toes, and using an emollient on dry skin but never between the toes (as cited earlier; not re-opened). Plain petroleum jelly does the job; urea creams are offered for thick, cracked heels.
why.sw: Kisukari hukausha ngozi ya miguu, na visigino vilivyopasuka huruhusu maambukizi kuingia kupitia ngozi ambayo huenda haisikii tena maumivu. Mwongozo wa IWGDF wa 2023 kuhusu kuzuia vidonda vya miguu unashauri kukagua miguu kila siku, kuosha na kukausha vizuri katikati ya vidole, na kupaka mafuta kwenye ngozi kavu lakini kamwe si katikati ya vidole. Mafuta ya kawaida ya petroli yanatosha; krimu zenye urea zinatolewa kwa visigino vigumu vilivyopasuka.

why.en: Sugar on the fingers from fruit or food gives a falsely high reading, so the right step before every finger prick is washing with soap and water and drying well. Spirit swabs are left out: soap and water is the method meter makers recommend, and spirit dries the fingertips.

name.en: Oral rehydration salts for sick days (partner pharmacy)
name.sw: Chumvi za kurejesha maji mwilini kwa siku za kuugua (famasia mshirika)

why.en: Diarrhoea, vomiting or fever is when diabetes turns dangerous: fluid loss pushes sugar up, and some tablets, such as metformin, may need to be paused while the body is dry. Sick-day rules are the clinic’s: keep drinking, test more often, and ask which tablets to stop. ORS is a medicine in Tanzania (R1), so the partner pharmacy supplies it; WHO low-osmolarity ORS is mixed exactly as the sachet says.
why.sw: Kuharisha, kutapika au homa ndipo kisukari kinapokuwa hatari: kupoteza maji husukuma sukari juu, na baadhi ya vidonge kama metformin huenda vikahitaji kusimamishwa mwili ukiwa umekauka. Kanuni za siku ya kuugua ni za kliniki: endelea kunywa, pima mara nyingi zaidi, na uliza vidonge vipi usimamishe. ORS ni dawa Tanzania, hivyo famasia mshirika ndiyo huitoa; ORS ya WHO huchanganywa sawasawa na maelekezo ya pakiti.

Yearly foot screen with a monofilament in store: free once staff are trained.
